extracted.intended_audience: researchers in computational complexity and finite model theory / logic in computer science
extracted.subtask_short: ESO Horn FO expressibility for clique
extracted.subtask_description: A research note on whether the decision version of the maximum clique problem can be expressed in existential second-order logic whose first-order part is Horn (with and without an ordering); includes a withdrawal explaining logical errors and limits of expressibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressibility of Maximum Clique in ESO with Horn FO
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum clique problem (decision version) can be expressed in existential second order (ESO) logic, where the first order part is a Horn formula in second-order quantified predicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original claim by the author; note that the manuscript was withdrawn because the results are incorrect. Use caution: the published abstract states this as the principal result but the author later retracts it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unordered-structure FO form: Π2 Horn
rubrics_metrics.description: Without ordering, the first-order part of the ESO formulation is claimed to be a Π2 Horn formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a structural claim about the quantifier/logic level when no linear order is available on the structure; its validity is questioned by the withdrawal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordered-structure FO form: universal Horn and polynomial determinability
rubrics_metrics.description: If ordering is used, then the first-order part can be universal Horn, in which case the second-order variables can be determined in polynomial time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links the presence of an order to a stronger (universal Horn) syntactic form and to algorithmic consequences (polytime detection of second-order witnesses). The withdrawal indicates these conclusions may not hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horn conjunction decomposition fallacy (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ = φ1 AND φ2, and φ is a Horn formula, it does NOT imply that both φ1 and φ2 are Horn formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an identified logical error that caused the author to withdraw the manuscript. It serves as a caution when reasoning by decomposing formulas: Hornness is not necessarily preserved under splitting a conjunction into conjuncts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-expressibility of cardinality constraint as universal Horn in ESO
rubrics_metrics.description: The cardinality constraint CANNOT be expressed as a universal Horn sentence in ESO (not even when the structure is ordered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation is asserted in the withdrawal comment and undermines attempts to encode cardinality constraints within universal Horn ESO formulations; relevant when trying to capture NP properties via restricted ESO fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Grädel's theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Grädel's theorem is valid at a lower (machine) level, but probably NOT at a higher level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cautionary note about applying Grädel's theorem: its correctness holds at a certain (low-level / machine) interpretation, but extrapolating it to higher-level syntactic or conceptual settings can be misleading.
